simple: the standard set of tables (and a small program language) through which firmware describes a PC's devices and power controls to the OS.
analogy: the floor plan and fuse-box pages of the inventory folder.
precise: the Advanced Configuration and Power Interface: a root pointer (RSDP), system description tables with a common 36-byte header and a byte checksum, fixed tables such as FADT, MADT, HPET and MCFG, and the DSDT/SSDT definition blocks containing AML bytecode the OS interprets.
source: D2 of F3-12 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum item 20): chapter on ACPI software programming model (RSDP, XSDT, the system description table header, FADT, MADT and its entry types, FPDT), and the separate HPET and MCFG table descriptions it references) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the signature format for Windows and UEFI program files.
analogy: the signed permission slip stapled to the back of the visitor's papers.
precise: a PKCS#7 SignedData structure, stored in the PE file's certificate table, whose signed content holds a hash of the image computed over the headers (excluding the checksum and the certificate-table entry) and the sections, but not over the certificate table itself.
source: D2 of F3-16 (Microsoft, "PE Format" (Microsoft Portable Executable and Common Object File Format Specification): optional header, data directories, the attribute certificate table) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D3 of F3-16 (Microsoft, "Windows Authenticode Portable Executable Signature Format": the Authenticode hash, SpcIndirectDataContent) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the phase that picks what to boot and starts it.
analogy: the timetable board.
precise: the phase that connects consoles and boot devices, reads the boot variables (BootOrder, Boot####), and loads and starts a boot option, falling back to defaults; in EDK II it is a DXE driver, BdsDxe.
source: D1 of F3-11 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Platform Initialization (PI) Specification" (curriculum item 13), Volume 1 (PEI: SEC hand-off, PEI core, PPIs, HOBs; the S3 resume path), Volume 2 (DXE core, dispatcher, BDS, the TSL/RT/AL phases), Volume 3 (Shared Architectural Elements: firmware volumes, firmware file system, file and section types, GUID-defined sections)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D2 of F3-11 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): boot manager, boot variables (BootOrder, Boot####), protocols and handles) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the original PC firmware, which starts in 16-bit mode and loads the first sector of a disk.
analogy: the old caretaker's routine on a card.
precise: the IBM PC-compatible Basic Input/Output System: firmware that initialises the platform, loads sector 0 of the boot device to 0000:7C00h, jumps to it in real mode, and provides services through software interrupts (INT 10h video, INT 13h disk, INT 15h system, among others).
source: D4 of F3-10 (Vincent Zimmer, Michael Rothman, Suresh Marisetty, "Beyond BIOS: Developing with the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface" (curriculum item 14), chapters on the legacy BIOS and on the transition to UEFI) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D6 of F3-10 (OSDev wiki (curriculum item 8), pages "Real Mode", "MBR (x86)", "Disk access using the BIOS (INT 13h)", "Detecting Memory (x86)" (E820), "UEFI" and "UEFI App Bare Bones", as named in milestones A1 and A5) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the record the loader fills in and passes to the kernel.
analogy: the folder handed over with the keys.
precise: a data structure in memory, whose address is passed to the kernel at entry, holding the hand-over data of a boot protocol; in OS301 it is os301::BootInfo, which starts with a magic number, a version and its own size.
source: S1 of F3-14 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 2.7 (boot protocols table: systemd-boot, Limine, Multiboot2, Linux x86 boot protocol, "UEFI handoff (your own)") and milestone A3 (goal, build list, acceptance tests quoted verbatim); a map, not a source)

simple: the program that loads the operating system's kernel into memory and starts it.
analogy: the person who unlocks the classroom and lets the principal in.
precise: software started by the firmware (here a UEFI application) that locates the kernel image and its inputs, loads them, collects platform information, puts the processor in the state the kernel's boot protocol requires and transfers control to the kernel's entry point.
source: D1 of F3-14 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): images and the OS loader's role, LoadImage and StartImage) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); S1 of F3-14 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 2.7 (boot protocols table: systemd-boot, Limine, Multiboot2, Linux x86 boot protocol, "UEFI handoff (your own)") and milestone A3 (goal, build list, acceptance tests quoted verbatim); a map, not a source)

simple: the written agreement between a loader and a kernel about how the kernel is started and what it receives.
analogy: the handover checklist both have signed.
precise: a specification of the kernel image format the loader accepts, the processor state at entry (mode, paging, registers, stack, interrupts) and the format and location of the information passed (memory map, framebuffer, firmware tables, command line, modules).
source: D3 of F3-14 (GNU (GRUB project), "Multiboot Specification" (version 0.6.96) and "Multiboot2 Specification" (curriculum item 18); the Limine boot protocol (curriculum item 17); the Linux kernel's x86 boot protocol documentation (curriculum section 2.7)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); S1 of F3-14 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 2.7 (boot protocols table: systemd-boot, Limine, Multiboot2, Linux x86 boot protocol, "UEFI handoff (your own)") and milestone A3 (goal, build list, acceptance tests quoted verbatim); a map, not a source)

simple: the first 512 bytes of a disk, which an old BIOS loads and runs.
analogy: the instructions taped inside the door of room 1.
precise: sector 0 of a disk; a legacy BIOS checks that bytes 510 and 511 are 55h and AAh, loads the sector to physical address 7C00h and jumps to it with the boot drive number in DL.
source: D4 of F3-10 (Vincent Zimmer, Michael Rothman, Suresh Marisetty, "Beyond BIOS: Developing with the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface" (curriculum item 14), chapters on the legacy BIOS and on the transition to UEFI) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D6 of F3-10 (OSDev wiki (curriculum item 8), pages "Real Mode", "MBR (x86)", "Disk access using the BIOS (INT 13h)", "Detecting Memory (x86)" (E820), "UEFI" and "UEFI App Bare Bones", as named in milestones A1 and A5) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two groups of firmware functions: one usable only while booting, one that stays available to the OS.
analogy: the tools on loan and the small office that stays open.
precise: function tables reached from the EFI system table; boot services (memory allocation, protocol lookup, image loading, ExitBootServices) end when the loader calls ExitBootServices; runtime services (variables, time, reset) remain callable by the OS.
source: D1 of F3-10 (UEFI Forum, "Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Specification" (curriculum item 12): sections "EFI System Table", "Boot Services" (memory allocation services, GetMemoryMap, memory types and attributes), "Runtime Services", "Simple Text Output Protocol", "Image Entry Point", the calling conventions for x64, the boot manager and "Removable Media Boot Behavior") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a list in the system table that pairs a GUID with the address of a table.
analogy: the folder's sticky tabs, each with a code.
precise: the array of EFI_CONFIGURATION_TABLE entries (vendor GUID, pointer) referenced by the EFI system table, through which firmware publishes the ACPI RSDP, SMBIOS entry points and other tables.
source: D1 of F3-12 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): "EFI System Table" and "EFI Configuration Table" (the ACPI 2.0 and SMBIOS GUIDs)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a 32-bit check value computed from a block of bytes; a changed byte gives a different value.
analogy: the check number at the bottom of the room plan.
precise: a cyclic redundancy check; the variant used by GPT is the reflected CRC with polynomial EDB88320h, initial value FFFFFFFFh and final inversion; it detects all single-bit and single-byte errors but is not a cryptographic protection.
source: D1 of F3-13 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): the chapter "GUID Partition Table (GPT) Disk Layout" (protective MBR, GPT header, partition entry array, backup structures, CRC32), the EFI System Partition and "Removable Media Boot Behavior") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F3-13 (lab run)

simple: two versions of the same firmware: one talkative and larger, one quiet and smaller.
analogy: the caretaker with the notebook, and the one without.
precise: build targets of EDK II (-b DEBUG or -b RELEASE); in a debug build the DEBUG and ASSERT macros produce output and checks, on OVMF written to an I/O port that QEMU can capture; in a release build they compile to nothing.
source: D1 of F3-17 (TianoCore, "EDK II Build Specification" and the "EDK II DSC, FDF and INF File Specifications"; OvmfPkg documentation in the EDK II tree (curriculum, milestone A4 reading list)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: Firmware volume (FV), firmware file (FFS) and section

simple: the phase where most firmware drivers run and the UEFI services appear.
analogy: switching on every classroom and corridor.
precise: the phase in which the DXE core builds the UEFI boot and runtime services, and a dispatcher loads DXE drivers from firmware volumes in dependency order; drivers install protocols for buses and devices and produce tables such as ACPI and SMBIOS.
source: D1 of F3-11 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Platform Initialization (PI) Specification" (curriculum item 13), Volume 1 (PEI: SEC hand-off, PEI core, PPIs, HOBs; the S3 resume path), Volume 2 (DXE core, dispatcher, BDS, the TSL/RT/AL phases), Volume 3 (Shared Architectural Elements: firmware volumes, firmware file system, file and section types, GUID-defined sections)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the open-source code base from which most UEFI firmware, including OVMF, is built.
analogy: the agency's book of standard procedures from which each caretaker's job description is assembled.
precise: the reference implementation of the UEFI and PI specifications, organised in packages (MdePkg, MdeModulePkg, OvmfPkg and others) of modules, built by its BaseTools build command from a platform description.
source: D1 of F3-17 (TianoCore, "EDK II Build Specification" and the "EDK II DSC, FDF and INF File Specifications"; OvmfPkg documentation in the EDK II tree (curriculum, milestone A4 reading list)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); S1 of F3-17 (Systems Curriculum (this project), milestone A4 (goal, build, acceptance quoted verbatim), section 2.3 (PI phases), section 2.5 (roots of trust, flashing retail PCs); a map, not a source)
related: Firmware volume (FV), firmware file (FFS) and section

simple: the partition, formatted FAT, where UEFI firmware looks for boot loaders.
analogy: the key cabinet by the entrance where the person who unlocks the classroom keeps the keys.
precise: a partition with the type GUID C12A7328-F81F-11D2-BA4B-00A0C93EC93B and a FAT file system that UEFI firmware must be able to read; it holds boot loaders, including the removable-media default \EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI on x86-64.
source: D1 of F3-13 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): the chapter "GUID Partition Table (GPT) Disk Layout" (protective MBR, GPT header, partition entry array, backup structures, CRC32), the EFI System Partition and "Removable Media Boot Behavior") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the standard file format for programs and kernels on Linux and many other systems.
analogy: a packing list on the box that says which item goes on which shelf.
precise: the Executable and Linkable Format: an ELF header (magic, class, data encoding, type, machine, entry point, table offsets) followed by a program-header table for loading and a section-header table for linking and debugging.
source: D2 of F3-14 (Tool Interface Standard (TIS) Committee, "Executable and Linking Format (ELF) Specification", and the System V gABI (curriculum item 5): ELF header, program header, PT_LOAD, segment permissions) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the call in which the loader tells the firmware "I take over now; stop your services".
analogy: the caretaker's handover at the end of the shift.
precise: the UEFI boot service ExitBootServices(ImageHandle, MapKey); if MapKey is the key of the current memory map, the firmware ends boot services and returns success, after which only runtime services may be used; otherwise it returns an error and boot services remain partly available.
source: D1 of F3-15 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): boot services GetMemoryMap, AllocatePages, AllocatePool, ExitBootServices; Loaded Image, Simple File System, File and Graphics Output protocols; the configuration table) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); S1 of F3-15 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 2.7 ("The ExitBootServices rule", quoted verbatim), section 2.2 (CPU mode at handoff) and milestone A3 (goal, build list, acceptance tests quoted verbatim); a map, not a source)

simple: the program stored on a chip on the motherboard that runs first when the machine is switched on.
analogy: the caretaker who opens the doors in the morning.
precise: software held in non-volatile memory (flash) on the platform that initialises the processor, memory and devices, describes the hardware to the operating system and loads an OS loader; on PCs it is UEFI firmware or, on older machines, a legacy BIOS.
source: D3 of F3-09 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Platform Initialization (PI) Specification" (curriculum item 13), Volume 1 (Pre-EFI Initialization Core Interface: the SEC and PEI phases, hand-off blocks) and Volume 2 (Driver Execution Environment Core Interface), overview sections on the boot phases) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D4 of F3-09 (Vincent Zimmer, Michael Rothman, Suresh Marisetty, "Beyond BIOS: Developing with the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface" (curriculum item 14), chapters on the platform initialization flow and on the PC's legacy heritage) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: Segment base (hidden part of a segment register)

term: Firmware volume (FV), firmware file (FFS) and section
simple: the boxes inside a firmware image: volumes hold files, files hold sections.
analogy: cupboards, folders in the cupboards, pages in the folders.
precise: an FV is a region with a header (signature "_FVH", length, header checksum) holding firmware files; each file has a 24-byte header with a GUID name, a type (SEC core, PEI core, PEIM, DXE core, driver, application, raw, volume image…) and a size; a file's data is a series of sections, some of which contain code, a user-interface name, compressed data or a whole nested volume.
source: D1 of F3-11 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Platform Initialization (PI) Specification" (curriculum item 13), Volume 1 (PEI: SEC hand-off, PEI core, PPIs, HOBs; the S3 resume path), Volume 2 (DXE core, dispatcher, BDS, the TSL/RT/AL phases), Volume 3 (Shared Architectural Elements: firmware volumes, firmware file system, file and section types, GUID-defined sections)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an ACPI table in which firmware records how long its own boot steps took.
analogy: the caretaker's time sheet for the morning round.
precise: the Firmware Performance Data Table, which points to performance records with time stamps for points such as the end of reset, the OS loader's load and start, and ExitBootServices entry and exit; tools that draw boot timelines (for example on Windows) read it.
source: D2 of F3-12 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum item 20): chapter on ACPI software programming model (RSDP, XSDT, the system description table header, FADT, MADT and its entry types, FPDT), and the separate HPET and MCFG table descriptions it references) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a door in QEMU that lets the GDB debugger stop and inspect the virtual processor.
analogy: a window into the building that lets an inspector watch the caretaker from the first step.
precise: QEMU's implementation of the GDB remote serial protocol (-gdb tcp:…, with -S to hold the CPU at reset), through which GDB reads registers and memory and single-steps the guest.
source: D5 of F3-09 (QEMU project, "QEMU System Emulation User's Documentation": GDB usage (-s, -S, -gdb), QEMU Monitor commands (info registers, xp, gva2gpa, stop), the pflash drive interface) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D6 of F3-09 (Free Software Foundation, "Debugging with GDB" (the GDB manual): chapters on remote debugging, examining memory (x) and continuing and stepping (stepi)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the modern partition table, stored twice on the disk with check values.
analogy: the room plan kept at the front entrance and at the back door.
precise: the UEFI partitioning scheme: a header at LBA 1 (signature "EFI PART", CRC32 of itself and of the entry array, its own and the alternate header's LBA, usable range, disk GUID) and an array of partition entries (type GUID, unique GUID, first and last LBA, attributes, UTF-16 name), mirrored by a backup array and backup header at the end of the disk.
source: D1 of F3-13 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): the chapter "GUID Partition Table (GPT) Disk Layout" (protective MBR, GPT header, partition entry array, backup structures, CRC32), the EFI System Partition and "Removable Media Boot Behavior") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the firmware's description of the screen: where its memory is and how big it is.
analogy: the caretaker's note about the notice board: where it hangs and how many rows it has.
precise: the UEFI protocol giving the current mode's resolution, pixel format, pixels per scan line, and the framebuffer's physical base and size; the framebuffer stays valid after ExitBootServices.
source: D1 of F3-15 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): boot services GetMemoryMap, AllocatePages, AllocatePool, ExitBootServices; Loaded Image, Simple File System, File and Graphics Output protocols; the configuration table) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a 128-bit number used as a name that nobody else will pick by accident.
analogy: a unique room code that cannot be confused with another school's.
precise: a globally unique identifier; UEFI names protocols, configuration tables and variable namespaces with GUIDs.
source: D1 of F3-10 (UEFI Forum, "Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Specification" (curriculum item 12): sections "EFI System Table", "Boot Services" (memory allocation services, GetMemoryMap, memory types and attributes), "Runtime Services", "Simple Text Output Protocol", "Image Entry Point", the calling conventions for x64, the boot manager and "Removable Media Boot Behavior") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a kernel linked to run at very large virtual addresses, leaving the low addresses for programs.
analogy: the staff offices on the top floor, the classrooms below.
precise: a kernel whose virtual addresses lie in the upper part of the canonical address space (here from 0xffffffff80000000, the range the x86-64 "kernel" code model assumes), mapped there by page tables regardless of where it sits in physical memory.
source: D4 of F3-14 (x86-64 psABI maintainers, "System V Application Binary Interface, AMD64 Architecture Processor Supplement" (curriculum item 6): calling convention (RDI first argument), code models (kernel), the red zone) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small record that PEI leaves for DXE: "here is memory", "here is a firmware volume".
analogy: a note pinned on the boiler-room door for whoever comes next.
precise: an entry in the HOB list, a sequence of typed, length-prefixed records built during PEI (resource descriptors, memory allocations, firmware-volume locations, GUID-identified data) and passed to the DXE core.
source: D1 of F3-11 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Platform Initialization (PI) Specification" (curriculum item 13), Volume 1 (PEI: SEC hand-off, PEI core, PPIs, HOBs; the S3 resume path), Volume 2 (DXE core, dispatcher, BDS, the TSL/RT/AL phases), Volume 3 (Shared Architectural Elements: firmware volumes, firmware file system, file and section types, GUID-defined sections)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a mapping where every virtual address equals the physical address.
analogy: the room numbers on the plan are the numbers on the doors.
precise: page-table entries mapping virtual address v to physical address v; the loader needs it because the instruction after mov cr3 is fetched at the same (identity-mapped, under the firmware) address.
source: D3 of F3-15 (Intel Corporation, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual", Volume 3, "Paging" chapter (4-level paging, entry formats, access rights) and the EFER description) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a sector's number on the disk, counting from 0.
analogy: the room number.
precise: the index of a logical block (here 512 bytes) in a linear numbering of the device; byte offset = LBA × block size.
source: D1 of F3-13 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): the chapter "GUID Partition Table (GPT) Disk Layout" (protective MBR, GPT header, partition entry array, backup structures, CRC32), the EFI System Partition and "Removable Media Boot Behavior") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the 64-bit mode the processor runs in once firmware or the OS has switched it on.
analogy: the full timetable in force, with every room numbered and locked.
precise: the x86-64 operating mode, active when EFER.LMA = 1, entered with paging enabled (CR0.PG), physical address extension (CR4.PAE) and EFER.LME set.
source: D1 of F3-09 (Intel Corporation, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual" (curriculum reading-list item 10), Volume 3 (System Programming Guide): the chapter on processor management and initialization (processor state after reset, first instruction executed, switching to protected mode and to IA-32e mode), the chapter on paging (4-level paging, page-structure entry formats, PS and NX bits) and the system-architecture overview (control registers CR0, CR3, CR4 and EFER)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D2 of F3-09 (Advanced Micro Devices, "AMD64 Architecture Programmer's Manual", Volume 2: System Programming (curriculum item 11), chapters on processor initialization and long-mode activation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the ACPI table that lists the processors and interrupt controllers.
analogy: the page saying which doorbell rings in which office.
precise: the Multiple APIC Description Table (signature "APIC"): the local APIC address followed by variable-length entries (processor local APIC, I/O APIC, interrupt source override, NMI and others).
source: D2 of F3-12 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum item 20): chapter on ACPI software programming model (RSDP, XSDT, the system description table header, FADT, MADT and its entry types, FPDT), and the separate HPET and MCFG table descriptions it references) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the old partition table: four entries inside the first 512-byte sector of a disk.
analogy: a room plan small enough to fit on the front door.
precise: four 16-byte entries at offset 446 of sector 0 (type byte, 32-bit starting LBA, 32-bit sector count and legacy CHS fields), followed by the 55h AAh signature; 32-bit LBAs limit it to 232 sectors.
source: D1 of F3-13 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): the chapter "GUID Partition Table (GPT) Disk Layout" (protective MBR, GPT header, partition entry array, backup structures, CRC32), the EFI System Partition and "Removable Media Boot Behavior") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D4 of F3-13 (Vincent Zimmer, Michael Rothman, Suresh Marisetty, "Beyond BIOS" (curriculum item 14), chapter on storage and the MBR heritage; and the OSDev wiki page "MBR (x86)" (curriculum item 8)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each step of the boot writes a fingerprint of the next step into a tamper-proof log before running it.
analogy: the visitors' book in ink.
precise: each boot component measures (hashes) the next one and extends a TPM Platform Configuration Register with that digest, and appends an event to the event log; the PCR values can be reported, signed by the TPM, to a remote verifier (attestation).
source: D4 of F3-16 (Trusted Computing Group, "TCG PC Client Platform Firmware Profile Specification": what is measured into which PCR, the event log) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); S1 of F3-16 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 2.5 "Security and hidden components" (Secure Boot, shim, MOK, measured boot, roots of trust; the exercise quoted verbatim); a map, not a source)

simple: the firmware's list of which physical address ranges are RAM and which are reserved.
analogy: the written list of every room and what it is for.
precise: UEFI's GetMemoryMap returns an array of descriptors (type, physical start, number of 4 KiB pages, attributes) plus a map key; the legacy equivalent is the list returned entry by entry by INT 15h with EAX = E820h (base, length, type).
source: D1 of F3-10 (UEFI Forum, "Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Specification" (curriculum item 12): sections "EFI System Table", "Boot Services" (memory allocation services, GetMemoryMap, memory types and attributes), "Runtime Services", "Simple Text Output Protocol", "Image Entry Point", the calling conventions for x64, the boot manager and "Removable Media Boot Behavior") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D6 of F3-10 (OSDev wiki (curriculum item 8), pages "Real Mode", "MBR (x86)", "Disk access using the BIOS (INT 13h)", "Detecting Memory (x86)" (E820), "UEFI" and "UEFI App Bare Bones", as named in milestones A1 and A5) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number the firmware gives with each memory map; it changes whenever memory is allocated or freed.
analogy: today's stamp on the room plan.
precise: the MapKey output of GetMemoryMap, identifying the state of the memory map at that moment; ExitBootServices accepts only the key of the current map.
source: D1 of F3-15 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): boot services GetMemoryMap, AllocatePages, AllocatePool, ExitBootServices; Loaded Image, Simple File System, File and Graphics Output protocols; the configuration table) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a UEFI firmware built for virtual machines such as QEMU.
analogy: a caretaker trained for a model school instead of a real one.
precise: the "Open Virtual Machine Firmware" platform of the EDK II project, which builds UEFI firmware images for QEMU and other hypervisors; this course uses the build shipped in the Ubuntu package ovmf 2024.02-2ubuntu0.10.
source: D7 of F3-09 (TianoCore community, EDK II documentation and source (curriculum item 16): OvmfPkg and the x86 reset-vector module) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F3-09 (lab run)

simple: the tables that turn the addresses a program uses into real memory addresses; CR3 holds where the top table is.
analogy: the map of lockers: locker number to real cupboard.
precise: on x86-64 with 4-level paging, a tree of 4 KiB tables (PML4, PDPT, PD, PT) of 512 eight-byte entries; bits 47–39, 38–30, 29–21 and 20–12 of a virtual address index the four levels; an entry with the PS bit set in the PDPT or PD maps a 1 GiB or 2 MiB page directly.
source: D1 of F3-09 (Intel Corporation, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual" (curriculum reading-list item 10), Volume 3 (System Programming Guide): the chapter on processor management and initialization (processor state after reset, first instruction executed, switching to protected mode and to IA-32e mode), the chapter on paging (4-level paging, page-structure entry formats, PS and NX bits) and the system-architecture overview (control registers CR0, CR3, CR4 and EFER)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the switches in each page-table entry that say whether the page exists, may be written, and may hold code.
analogy: the signs on a classroom door: "open", "staff may rearrange", "no lessons held here".
precise: in x86-64 four-level paging, bit 0 Present, bit 1 Read/Write, bit 7 Page Size (2 MiB or 1 GiB page at levels 2 and 3), bit 63 Execute-Disable (honoured when EFER.NXE = 1); the physical address of the next table or the page is in bits 12 to 51.
source: D3 of F3-15 (Intel Corporation, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual", Volume 3, "Paging" chapter (4-level paging, entry formats, access rights) and the EFER description) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the program coreboot starts after it has set up the hardware: the part that actually finds and boots an operating system.
analogy: a caretaker who only unlocks the gates and switches on the heating, then hands over to a receptionist who takes visitors to their rooms.
precise: a program loaded by coreboot's last stage (ramstage), for example SeaBIOS, an EDK II payload (a UEFI implementation) or LinuxBoot; coreboot's stages are bootblock, romstage, postcar and ramstage.
source: S1 of F3-17 (Systems Curriculum (this project), milestone A4 (goal, build, acceptance quoted verbatim), section 2.3 (PI phases), section 2.5 (roots of trust, flashing retail PCs); a map, not a source)
related: Firmware volume (FV), firmware file (FFS) and section

simple: the only way to change a TPM register: mix in a new value, never set it.
analogy: adding a line to the book; there is no eraser.
precise: PCRnew = H(PCRold ‖ digest) for the PCR bank's hash H (SHA-256 here); the final value depends on every digest and their order, and the register can only return to its initial value by a platform reset.
source: D5 of F3-16 (Trusted Computing Group, "TPM 2.0 Library Specification" (Part 1, Architecture): PCRs, extend, quotes) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the 64-bit Windows executable file format, which UEFI also uses for its programs.
analogy: the standard form every visitor must fill in at the desk.
precise: the Portable Executable format with the optional-header magic 0x20B (64-bit); UEFI images use it with subsystem values for applications and drivers.
source: D1 of F3-10 (UEFI Forum, "Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Specification" (curriculum item 12): sections "EFI System Table", "Boot Services" (memory allocation services, GetMemoryMap, memory types and attributes), "Runtime Services", "Simple Text Output Protocol", "Image Entry Point", the calling conventions for x64, the boot manager and "Removable Media Boot Behavior") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D7 of F3-10 (Microsoft, PE/COFF specification ("PE Format": optional header magic, subsystem values, base relocations; x64 calling convention)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F3-10 (lab run)

simple: the phase that makes the real memory work.
analogy: the boiler room: nothing else is usable until it runs.
precise: a small dispatcher (the PEI core) that runs PEI modules (PEIMs) in dependency order, with interfaces called PPIs; its main duties are initialising permanent memory and describing the platform in hand-off blocks (HOBs) for DXE.
source: D1 of F3-11 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Platform Initialization (PI) Specification" (curriculum item 13), Volume 1 (PEI: SEC hand-off, PEI core, PPIs, HOBs; the S3 resume path), Volume 2 (DXE core, dispatcher, BDS, the TSL/RT/AL phases), Volume 3 (Shared Architectural Elements: firmware volumes, firmware file system, file and section types, GUID-defined sections)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the standard for how UEFI firmware itself is built inside: its phases and its module formats.
analogy: the written order of the caretaker's morning round.
precise: the UEFI Forum's Platform Initialization Specification, which defines the boot phases (SEC, PEI, DXE, BDS and later ones), the interfaces between modules in each phase, and the firmware storage format; the UEFI Specification defines what the OS loader sees, PI defines how the firmware gets there.
source: D1 of F3-11 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Platform Initialization (PI) Specification" (curriculum item 13), Volume 1 (PEI: SEC hand-off, PEI core, PPIs, HOBs; the S3 resume path), Volume 2 (DXE core, dispatcher, BDS, the TSL/RT/AL phases), Volume 3 (Shared Architectural Elements: firmware volumes, firmware file system, file and section types, GUID-defined sections)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two text files that say which modules go into a firmware and where in the flash image they are placed.
analogy: the job description (what he does) and the floor plan of his key cabinet (where each key hangs).
precise: the DSC file lists the modules to build, the libraries they use and the build-time settings (PCDs); the FDF file lists the firmware volumes and which built modules go into each; each module has its own INF description.
source: D1 of F3-17 (TianoCore, "EDK II Build Specification" and the "EDK II DSC, FDF and INF File Specifications"; OvmfPkg documentation in the EDK II tree (curriculum, milestone A4 reading list)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: Firmware volume (FV), firmware file (FFS) and section

simple: a fake MBR on a GPT disk that tells old tools "this disk is in use".
analogy: a sign on the front door: "plan inside, do not draw a new one".
precise: an MBR in sector 0 of a GPT disk whose single partition entry has type EEh, starts at LBA 1 and covers the disk (or as much as 32 bits allow).
source: D1 of F3-13 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): the chapter "GUID Partition Table (GPT) Disk Layout" (protective MBR, GPT header, partition entry array, backup structures, CRC32), the EFI System Partition and "Removable Media Boot Behavior") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one piece of the file that the loader must put in memory.
analogy: one line of the packing list: "these items, to that shelf, in a locked or open cupboard".
precise: a program-header entry of type PT_LOAD giving the file offset and size (p_offset, p_filesz), the virtual address and memory size (p_vaddr, p_memsz; the bytes beyond p_filesz are zero, which is how .bss is stored) and the permission flags R, W, X.
source: D2 of F3-14 (Tool Interface Standard (TIS) Committee, "Executable and Linking Format (ELF) Specification", and the System V gABI (curriculum item 5): ELF header, program header, PT_LOAD, segment permissions) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the old 16-bit way the processor starts, with no memory protection.
analogy: the building before any room has a lock.
precise: the 8086-compatible operating mode an x86 processor enters at reset: 16-bit instructions by default, addresses formed as segment base plus offset, no paging and no privilege checks.
source: D1 of F3-09 (Intel Corporation, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual" (curriculum reading-list item 10), Volume 3 (System Programming Guide): the chapter on processor management and initialization (processor state after reset, first instruction executed, switching to protected mode and to IA-32e mode), the chapter on paging (4-level paging, page-structure entry formats, PS and NX bits) and the system-architecture overview (control registers CR0, CR3, CR4 and EFER)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: Segment base (hidden part of a segment register)

simple: a build that gives exactly the same output bytes every time it is run on the same source.
analogy: two copies of the visitors' book entry written from the same facts that read letter for letter the same.
precise: a build process whose output is a deterministic function of its inputs (source, tool versions, options), with no time stamps, paths or other environment data embedded; required when a measurement (hash) of the built file is compared with an expected value. In F3-16, lld-link wrote a time stamp into the PE header unless /Brepro was given.
source: R10 of F3-16 (lab run: two links of the same object file, with and without /Brepro)

simple: the fixed address where the processor fetches its first instruction after reset.
analogy: the one door the caretaker always enters by.
precise: on x86, physical address FFFFFFF0h: the processor starts in real-address mode with CS selector F000h, a hidden CS base of FFFF0000h and IP 0000FFF0h; platform logic maps the top of the firmware flash there.
source: D1 of F3-09 (Intel Corporation, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual" (curriculum reading-list item 10), Volume 3 (System Programming Guide): the chapter on processor management and initialization (processor state after reset, first instruction executed, switching to protected mode and to IA-32e mode), the chapter on paging (4-level paging, page-structure entry formats, PS and NX bits) and the system-architecture overview (control registers CR0, CR3, CR4 and EFER)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R3 of F3-09 (lab run)
related: Segment base (hidden part of a segment register)

simple: the first pointer and the table of contents of the ACPI tables.
analogy: the folder's cover page and its index.
precise: the Root System Description Pointer (signature "RSD PTR ", checksums over its first 20 bytes and, for revision 2 and later, over its full length) holds the physical address of the Extended System Description Table, whose body is an array of 64-bit physical addresses of the other tables.
source: D2 of F3-12 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum item 20): chapter on ACPI software programming model (RSDP, XSDT, the system description table header, FADT, MADT and its entry types, FPDT), and the separate HPET and MCFG table descriptions it references) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F3-12 (lab run)

simple: the first firmware code after reset; it sets up temporary memory and finds the next phase.
analogy: the front door and the alarm panel.
precise: the phase that handles the reset, establishes a temporary memory store (cache-as-RAM on real processors), may act as the root of trust, and passes control and a description of the temporary memory to the PEI core.
source: D1 of F3-11 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Platform Initialization (PI) Specification" (curriculum item 13), Volume 1 (PEI: SEC hand-off, PEI core, PPIs, HOBs; the S3 resume path), Volume 2 (DXE core, dispatcher, BDS, the TSL/RT/AL phases), Volume 3 (Shared Architectural Elements: firmware volumes, firmware file system, file and section types, GUID-defined sections)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the firmware feature that only starts programs signed by someone it trusts.
analogy: the caretaker who checks permission slips against the list in the staff room.
precise: UEFI image verification: before starting a UEFI image, the firmware checks its Authenticode signature (or its hash) against the allowed database db and the forbidden database dbx; db and dbx may be changed only with a signature from a Key Exchange Key (KEK), and the KEKs only with the Platform Key (PK).
source: D1 of F3-16 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): "Secure Boot and Driver Signing", "Globally Defined Variables", EFI_SIGNATURE_LIST, GetVariable, LoadImage) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); S1 of F3-16 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 2.5 "Security and hidden components" (Secure Boot, shim, MOK, measured boot, roots of trust; the exercise quoted verbatim); a map, not a source)

term: Segment base (hidden part of a segment register)
simple: a starting address the processor keeps next to each segment register, which it adds to every offset.
analogy: the floor number added to every room number.
precise: the base field of a segment register's descriptor cache; in real mode loading a selector sets base = selector × 16, but after reset CS has selector F000h with base FFFF0000h until the first far jump reloads it.
source: D1 of F3-09 (Intel Corporation, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual" (curriculum reading-list item 10), Volume 3 (System Programming Guide): the chapter on processor management and initialization (processor state after reset, first instruction executed, switching to protected mode and to IA-32e mode), the chapter on paging (4-level paging, page-structure entry formats, PS and NX bits) and the system-architecture overview (control registers CR0, CR3, CR4 and EFER)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: whether the platform has an owner key yet.
analogy: a school without a head of the board accepts any new list; once one is appointed, only signed changes count.
precise: with no PK enrolled the platform is in setup mode (variable SetupMode = 1), the key variables can be written without authentication and images are not verified; enrolling a PK switches to user mode, where SecureBoot = 1 if verification is enabled.
source: D1 of F3-16 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Specification" (curriculum item 12): "Secure Boot and Driver Signing", "Globally Defined Variables", EFI_SIGNATURE_LIST, GetVariable, LoadImage) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small first loader that Linux distributions use to boot with Secure Boot on.
analogy: a visitor with a permission slip from the board who vouches for his own colleagues.
precise: a UEFI loader signed by Microsoft's UEFI CA, which is in db on most PCs; it carries the distribution's own certificate and supports Machine Owner Keys (MOK), and verifies the next stage (for example GRUB) itself.
source: S1 of F3-16 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 2.5 "Security and hidden components" (Secure Boot, shim, MOK, measured boot, roots of trust; the exercise quoted verbatim); a map, not a source)

simple: the firmware's inventory of the machine: maker, model, firmware version, processor sockets, memory modules.
analogy: the page with the building's make and year.
precise: the System Management BIOS structure table: typed structures (type, length, handle, formatted area) each followed by a set of zero-terminated strings ending in an extra zero, found through a 32-bit or 64-bit ("_SM3_") entry point.
source: D3 of F3-12 (DMTF, "System Management BIOS (SMBIOS) Reference Specification" (curriculum item 21): the 64-bit entry point, the structure header and string set, types 0, 1, 4, 17 and 127) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a hidden processor mode where firmware code runs out of sight of the operating system.
analogy: a locked office in the school that only the caretaker can enter, even after he has handed over the building.
precise: an x86 operating mode entered through a System Management Interrupt, running code from protected memory (SMRAM) that the operating system cannot read or write; PI calls the software model for it MM (Management Mode), and its modules have the file types MM and MM_CORE.
source: D2 of F3-17 (UEFI Forum, "UEFI Platform Initialization (PI) Specification", Volumes 1–2 and Volume 4 (Management Mode)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); S1 of F3-17 (Systems Curriculum (this project), milestone A4 (goal, build, acceptance quoted verbatim), section 2.3 (PI phases), section 2.5 (roots of trust, flashing retail PCs); a map, not a source)
related: Firmware volume (FV), firmware file (FFS) and section

simple: a counter inside the processor that increases steadily; reading it twice tells how much time passed.
analogy: the school clock read at two moments.
precise: a 64-bit counter read with RDTSC; on current processors it increments at a constant rate, which must be calibrated against a known timer before converting counts to seconds.
source: D4 of F3-12 (Intel Corporation, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual", Volume 3: the time-stamp counter (RDTSC, invariant TSC)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the modern PC firmware standard; it starts programs stored as files and offers them services in tables.
analogy: the new front desk with a directory and tools on loan.
precise: the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface, a specification of the interface between firmware and OS loaders: a system table with boot services and runtime services, protocols identified by GUIDs, a boot manager driven by variables, and PE32+ images as the executable format.
source: D1 of F3-10 (UEFI Forum, "Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Specification" (curriculum item 12): sections "EFI System Table", "Boot Services" (memory allocation services, GetMemoryMap, memory types and attributes), "Runtime Services", "Simple Text Output Protocol", "Image Entry Point", the calling conventions for x64, the boot manager and "Removable Media Boot Behavior") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
